messages:
alice-customer: Hey team — since this morning we see a bunch of 429s and big p99 latency spikes when our product does short embedding calls in bursts. Happens only on bursts (~50 reqs/s) and only for small payloads. No errors in our side, request ids: req=acme-req-3201, acme-req-3202. Any quick checks?
jordan: Sorry about that — can you paste a raw curl example of one of the failing calls and a sample response headers (x-rate-limit / x-request-id)? Also which region and model?
alice-customer: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"short text"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings?model=text-mini
Response headers: x-request-id: acme-req-3201, x-rate-limit-remaining: 280, x-rate-limit-reset: 1680000, got HTTP 429 body: {"error":"quota_exceeded"}. Region: us-west-2.
sam: Thanks. Two quick possibilities: 1) quota exhaustion (global per-account burst quota) or 2) perceived throttling from our continuous batching/KV cache interactions — small requests can wait inside the batch window while the KV cache warms and appear as throttles. Can you confirm if these calls are cold keys (first time prefixes)?
alice-customer: They are mostly new user prefixes so likely cold. We also started a deploy yesterday that changed prefixing logic.
tara: If they're cold keys, you can see a spike in KV_CACHE_MISS in our runtime logs. Also, continuous batching will hold requests for up to the batching window (default 20ms) to form larger batches; for tiny requests that adds latency and under high concurrency can push queue depth which looks like throttling.
lee: Can you grab the response headers next time and share x-batching-window-ms and x-inference-queue-ms? Those will show queuing versus immediate 429. Also check x-kv-cache: miss|hit.
ops-bot: LOG STREAM snippet 2026-02-12T15:23:10Z: [node-42] REQ acme-req-3201 KV_CACHE_MISS batch_wait_ms=18 batch_size=12 queue_time_ms=42 instantiate_attempts=1 -> 429 quota_exhaustion
jordan: Nice logs, that suggests requests waited in batch queue and then failed when global burst quota hit. Short term: reduce client concurrency, add jitter, or switch to embeddings with a higher burst quota. Medium term: we can increase your burst quota for embeddings or move you to a dedicated pool.
sam: For repro you can run this small script to simulate cold-key bursts and toggle batching window:

# simulate (pseudo)
for i in 1..200 do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer X" -d '{"input":"u'${i}'"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings?model=text-mini &
done

sam: If you want to test toggling batching on our side, try adding header X-TEST-BATCHING: window_ms=0 (we'll only honor for test tokens) — that will bypass the batch hold and show pure per-request latency.
ale: We can also try prefetching keys on your warmup path: call a lightweight prefix-only embedding to prime KV cache before heavy bursts. That often removes the extra batch stalls.
jordan: Action items: 1) alice do a small repro with headers (x-batching-window-ms/x-inference-queue-ms/x-kv-cache). 2) we'll run a short quota bump for your account and monitor. 3) if warmup is needed we can share a prefetch pattern snippet. If results still bad I'll escalate to eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
